rows.basis: published by the Fed (what issuers owe minus what holders were found with)
rows.flow_code: derived: issuers' net issuance minus holders' net purchases

source: Federal Reserve Board, Financial Accounts of the United States (Z.1), table F2_2_s (amounts outstanding) and F2_2_t_tu (transactions, not seasonally adjusted), one line per holding sector
note: The share of each owner is of everything outstanding. Net bought is the Federal Reserve's quarterly net purchases; price and other changes is the change in holdings minus what was bought, which is mostly price moves. The Fed carries Treasury, agency, municipal and corporate bond totals at face value and most holders at market value, which is part of its published gap. Checkable deposits and currency are money that can be spent at once: notes and coin outside the banks, and deposits that can be drawn by cheque or card. What is owed is the Treasury's and the Federal Reserve's currency plus the banks' and credit unions' checkable deposits; the Fed's gap here is cheques in the post. This book is money, so it is not added into the world ledger's total of owned wealth.
